canvas-01.description: The east side of Emerson at 100 feet to an inch, drawn as an L around the key map that fills the upper right of the sheet. The upper arm covers the blocks between Belmont Avenue (and the edge of High Street) and Nassau Street from Jefferson Avenue south through Broad Street, Main Street, Linden Avenue and Ackerman Avenue to Hillside Avenue, with Union Avenue and Clinton Avenue running north-south; an unnamed 40 ft street divides blocks 59 and 60 and 65 and 64. At the top left Linwood Avenue curves in to meet Main Street. The lower arm runs along the foot of the sheet from the High Street side east to Fifth Street, covering Palisade Avenue, Randolph Avenue and Auricchio Avenue, crossed by Union Avenue and First to Fifth Streets. The area is almost entirely residential: narrow numbered building lots, most still vacant, with scattered frame dwellings and auto sheds, a few concrete-block and brick dwellings, hen houses, a work house on Jefferson Avenue and a tool house on Randolph Avenue. Blocks are numbered 1 to 17 and 22 to 41 and 59 to 65, and large unsubdivided lots remain south of Randolph Avenue (block 42) and east of Nassau Street (block 64). Six-inch water pipes are drawn in Main Street, Palisade Avenue, Randolph Avenue and First Street, with hydrants and an alarm tire. The key map, water facilities and fire department notes, the map key, the Sanborn cartouche (population 1100), a New Jersey location map and the index of specials occupy the framed upper right and are not part of the georeferenced area.
notes: Union Avenue north of Main Street is modern Samuel Street; south of Main Street it is Union Street.
The unnamed 40 ft street between blocks 59 and 60 and Clinton Avenue south of Main Street are both modern Clinton Street.
Linden Avenue, Ackerman Avenue and Hillside Avenue east of High Street are now Henry Street, East Ackerman Avenue and Marianna Place.
The key map, notes, legend, location map and specials index in the framed upper right are cut out of the mask.
Copyright 1924 by the Sanborn Map Co.; received stamp Aug 23 1924.

Sheet 1, 100 ft to an inch. Upper right is the key map of the borough (1300 ft to an inch), water and fire notes, the legend and the specials index, enclosed by a heavy line; these are cut out of the mask. The map is an L: the east side of town from Jefferson Av to Hillside Av between Belmont/High St and Nassau St, and along the foot of the sheet Palisade, Randolph and Auricchio Avs from High St to 5th St. One part. Union Av north of Main is modern Samuel Street; the unnamed 40 ft street between blocks 59/60 and 65/64 is modern Clinton Street; Clinton Av is Clinton Street; Linden, Ackerman and Hillside Avs (east of High St) are Henry Street, East Ackerman Avenue and Marianna Place.

sheet-2-1.description: The west side of Emerson, west of the New York and New Jersey Railroad (Erie Line), at 100 feet to an inch. At the top, Chestnut, Walnut, Lozier Avenue and Hillside Avenue are crossed by Grand Boulevard, an unnamed street north of Lozier Avenue and Dean; blocks 73, 74, 82, 83 and 84 are laid out in narrow numbered lots with only a few frame dwellings. Most of the middle of the sheet, between Hillside Avenue and Linwood Avenue, is a large undivided tract (block 72, lots 8 and 9) left blank. The lower third is the developed part: Linwood Avenue and Ackerman Avenue crossed by Campbell Avenue, Wortendyke Avenue and Hasbrouck Avenue, and a short stretch of Main Street beside the railroad; then south of Ackerman Avenue a regular grid of long blocks (93 to 101) along Kensington, Hollywood, Pavonia and Prospect Avenues, Campbell, Wortendyke and Hasbrouck Avenues, ending at Etna Avenue and Kinderkamack Road. The German Lutheran Church stands on Linwood Avenue at Hasbrouck Avenue (block 87). Along Main Street beside the tracks are stores and a concrete-block store building and a brick store (block 91). The rest is frame dwellings, auto sheds and hen houses, many of them on large lots west of Campbell Avenue. Six-inch and eight-inch water pipes run in Ackerman, Linwood and Hasbrouck Avenues and Kinderkamack Road. A north arrow and the scale bar sit in the blank west part of the sheet.
notes: Walnut is modern Birch Street; Campbell Avenue is the south part of Grand Boulevard; the street lettered 'Not named' north of Lozier Avenue is the north part of Hasbrouck Avenue.
Main Street west of the railroad is now part of Kinderkamack Road.
Dean has no modern counterpart in OpenStreetMap; Lincoln Boulevard now crosses the blank tract between Hillside and Linwood Avenues.
German Lutheran Church, Linwood Avenue at Hasbrouck Avenue.
Block 70 east of the railroad at the upper right continues in the inset at the upper left (match line A-B).

Sheet 2, 100 ft to an inch. Part 1 (main): the west side of the railroad from Chestnut St to Etna Av, Kensington Av to the Erie line, with a large blank tract between Hillside Av and Linwood Av. Part 2 (inset, upper left, inside a heavy frame): Kinderkamack Rd from Hartland Av to Highland Av east of the railroad, with Orchard Av, Allan and the west end of Chestnut (Chestnut Avenue). Walnut is modern Birch Street; Campbell Av is the south part of Grand Boulevard; the street lettered 'Not named' north of Lozier is Hasbrouck Avenue.

sheet-2-2.description: Inset in a heavy frame at the upper left of sheet 2, at 100 feet to an inch, showing the area east of the railroad along Kinderkamack Road between Hartland Avenue and Highland Avenue, north of the blocks on sheet 3. Kinderkamack Road runs down the inset with an eight-inch water pipe; Hartland Avenue runs along the top and Orchard Avenue and Highland Avenue cross east of the road, with Allan running between Orchard and Highland Avenues. Blocks 47, 48, 49 and 67 east of the road are cut into narrow numbered lots with a handful of frame dwellings and auto sheds. West of Kinderkamack Road the inset shows blocks 69 and 70 on either side of Chestnut, with frame dwellings on large lots and a hen house; a dash-dot match line A-B at the left edge joins this area to block 70 shown east of the railroad on the main part of the sheet. The inset is entirely residential.
notes: Chestnut west of Kinderkamack Road is modern Chestnut Avenue.
Allan has no modern counterpart in OpenStreetMap; the same junction with Highland Avenue is drawn on sheet 3 and was used to carry a control point.
Inset placed by four junctions along Kinderkamack Road plus the Allan / Highland Avenue point carried from sheet 3; lower confidence than the main parts.

Sheet 2, 100 ft to an inch. Part 1 (main): the west side of the railroad from Chestnut St to Etna Av, Kensington Av to the Erie line, with a large blank tract between Hillside Av and Linwood Av. Part 2 (inset, upper left, inside a heavy frame): Kinderkamack Rd from Hartland Av to Highland Av east of the railroad, with Orchard Av, Allan and the west end of Chestnut (Chestnut Avenue). Walnut is modern Birch Street; Campbell Av is the south part of Grand Boulevard; the street lettered 'Not named' north of Lozier is Hasbrouck Avenue.

sheet-3.description: The centre of Emerson at 100 feet to an inch, east of the New York and New Jersey Railroad (Erie Line). Kinderkamack Road runs diagonally down the left of the sheet from Highland Avenue to Linwood Avenue; east of it Dyer Avenue, Jefferson Avenue, Locust Avenue and Linwood Avenue run across the sheet to Belmont Avenue, crossed by Allan, Arthur Street and High Street, with Broad Street and Main Street at the right. Railroad Avenue runs south beside the tracks to Palisade Avenue at the foot. The railroad passenger station stands in a triangle by the tracks, with the Emerson Hotel and a dance hall on Railroad Avenue. Public buildings are the fire department (concrete block, on Locust Avenue), Union Church on Locust Avenue, the Church of the Assumption on Linwood Avenue and the brick and frame Emerson Public School on Linwood Avenue. Stores and gasoline tanks are at Kinderkamack Road and Linwood Avenue. West of the railroad is a narrow strip with Main Street, Lozier Avenue, Ackerman Avenue, Etna Avenue and Kinderkamack Road south of Ackerman Avenue, with dwellings in block 95. The rest is frame dwellings, auto sheds and hen houses, with long rows of narrow numbered lots on Dyer Avenue (blocks 51 and 52) and large undivided lots south of Linwood Avenue (block 56). The right edge shows the outline of sheet 1 with Linden, Ackerman and Hillside Avenues lettered, which is cut out of the mask.
notes: Railroad Avenue is modern Emerson Plaza East; Main Street west of the railroad is now Kinderkamack Road.
High Street ends at Linwood Avenue and does not continue north of Jefferson Avenue; both extensions are modern.
Allan has no modern counterpart in OpenStreetMap.
Specials on this sheet: Emerson Hotel, Emerson Public School, fire department, Union Church, Church of the Assumption, railroad station.
The outline of sheet 1 at the right (Linden, Ackerman and Hillside Avenues) and most of the scale bar are cut out of the mask.

Sheet 3, 100 ft to an inch. The centre of Emerson east of the railroad: Highland Av to Palisade Av, Kinderkamack Rd to Belmont Av, with the station, Emerson Hotel, public school, fire house and churches. West of the railroad a strip with Main St (now Kinderkamack Road) and Kinderkamack Rd south of Ackerman. The area east of High St south of Main is the outline of sheet 1 and is cut out of the mask; the west end of the scale bar, printed on a blank lot, is left in. One part. Railroad Av is now Emerson Plaza East; High St south of Linwood and north of Jefferson was not yet laid out.
